newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees W.European sugar crop little changed.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees W.European sugar crop little changed.

text.p: Europe's 1997-98 sugar harvest may only be marginally lower than last year, according to German statistician F.O. Licht.

"Thanks to the higher crop in Turkey, total west European sugar production is expected to remain largely unchanged from last year's 20.7 million tonnes, raw value," Licht said in its International Sugar and Sweetener Report.

Licht put total 1997-98 western European beet sugar production at 20.434 million tonnes raw value, compared with 20.652 million tonnes in 1996-97. EU production was put at 17.665 million tonnes (17.961 million), and eastern European production at 8.871 million tonnes (9.671 million)
"No shortage of high quality whites seems to be in sight especially in view of the fact that the export markets could become more difficult," Licht said.
Licht noted a general assumption that EU sugar production would be down, given last year's high yields and an almost unchanged sown area.

A reduction in area was likely to mean lower production in Eastern Europe. But import requirements would not rise as production in Russia, the biggest importer, was likely to be little changed, Licht said.
